propositions: The AC1 cross-surface equivalence contract re-calls the shared composer with identical arguments for MCP and reconciler surfaces instead of driving the real entry points, making the test vacuously true and unable to catch parity bugs.

The MCP and reconciler surface blocks must invoke their real entry points (build_server + call_tool, and main with argv) and capture the actual composed snapshots rather than re-composing through test code.

Each surface block must anchor to absolute expected content (repo root, envelope version, config keys with distinct provenance) and verify the recorder fired, so a surface that stops routing through the composer fails explicitly rather than silently looping over nothing.

The shared input must move from cli_overrides to project and environment layers so MCP and reconciler surfaces can be asserted without accepting cli arguments, which was why the original block re-composed instead of driving.
